text:
Maya: quick one — seeing a bunch of 413s on /v1/embeddings when clients send a mixed set of vectors (different lengths) in a single batch. SDK used to pack things aggressively, but the gateway now rejects with payload too large. Anyone know if we intentionally changed semantics? :thinking_face:

Liam H: we never intended to accept mixed-dim payloads as a single logical batch. The contract historically assumed uniform vector_length per request. That said, server used to silently pad/truncate in some runtimes, so behavior was fuzzy. We've tightened body-size checks which exposes the mismatch as 413s.

Sophie R: we should return a clearer error instead of 413. 413 is ambiguous (actual bytes vs semantic mismatch). Suggest a 400 with code `invalid_vector_length` and payload like `{"expected":1536,"found":[1536,128,1536]}` so clients can auto-split. Also add an example in the SDK error mapping.

Maya: +1. Customers are getting noisy alerts. They can't easily tell whether they hit a per-request byte limit or mixed-dims.

Liam H: agree on a specific code. Two engineering notes: (1) we need a cheap pre-parse check at the gateway to avoid expensive model routing work; (2) we must ensure telemetry captures both the semantic mismatch and the raw payload_size for quota accounting.

Sophie R: example error payload I propose:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_vector_length",
    "message": "Request contains multiple embedding lengths",
    "expected_vector_length": 1536,
    "per_item_lengths": [1536,128,1536],
    "suggestion": "split into uniform requests or use SDK auto-split"
  }
}
```

Andre P: telemetry + quotas convo — we currently count `embedding_units` per request as `num_items * (vector_length / 1024)` (rounded). Mixed dims break that formula. We have two options: compute per-item cost and sum (preferred), or deny mixed dims. Per-item cost will require payload inspection before routing. Slight perf hit but doable at gateway.

Liam H: per-item cost math makes sense. If we add a `vector_length` header (client-declared) we can short-circuit for the common uniform case and avoid deep-parsing. If header absent, gateway falls back to item-level scan.

Maya: how about SDKs defaulting to set `X-Vector-Length` for single-model embedding calls? That would keep perf for 95% of calls and only scan the rest. Also we must document rate/quotas clearly in Console.

Sophie R: Console change: add a per-route tile that shows `embed_units_consumed` and a small histogram of `vector_length` distribution. Also a new error-card that surfaces `invalid_vector_length` with example offending payload hashes so customers can correlate.

Andre P: implementation plan: (a) add gateway pre-parser that reads `X-Vector-Length` if present; (b) if missing, scan the JSON input and compute per-item lengths to produce `embed_units` metric; (c) emit telemetry events: `embed.request.start`, `embed.dim_mismatch`, `embed.quota.charge` with fields `num_items`, `vector_lengths`, `bytes`. We'll need to version the telemetry schema.

Sophie R: telemetry event names look good. Can we include `route_id` and `model_variant` for routing policy debug? Otherwise tracing from logs to billing is painful.

Liam H: yes include `route_id` and `model_variant`. Also add a boolean `used_client_header` so we can measure SDK adoption.

Maya: rollout plan proposal — gate the new strict error and telemetry under a feature flag `embed.dim_validation`. Start with 10% traffic on dedicated + hosted for 48h, check dim_mismatch rates, console error noise, and quota billing diffs. Then 50% for 24h, then 100%. For private/on-prem we ship as opt-in config.

Andre P: note: billing must not change mid-rollout. We'll send equivalent `embed_units` values even if we change how we compute them; only switch billing after we reconcile historical deltas and announce to customers.

Deploy Bot: deploy triggered: `feat/embed-dim-validate` -> canary @10% (start 1769994300), target finish 1769998600. :rocket:

Telemetry Bot: sample event emitted:
`{event: "embed.dim_mismatch", route_id: "rl-123", model_variant: "text-embed-3b/q1", vector_lengths: [1536,128,1536], bytes: 98342}`

Sophie R: UX follow-up — add a compact quickfix in Console that offers to "auto-split offending request" (calls the SDK helper) so support can triage. Small button, logs the split attempt.

Liam H: concerning SDK split: keep splits deterministic and preserve ordering metadata (client-provided id per item). Also provide a `split_hint` param so we can prefer size-based vs item-count-based splits.

Maya: ok action items: Sophie add console mock + error copy; Andre implement gateway pre-parser + telemetry events; Liam add header short-circuit + SDK change; I'll own rollout orchestration and customer comms.

Andre P: I'll start a tiny RFC on infra changes and link the gateway perf numbers. Expect PR by EOD.

Maya: thanks team — appreciate the quick sync. :thumbsup:
